mainTopic: Bathing, drying, and healing activities on שבת: towels, wearing garments, oiling, the baths of דיומסת, scraping, vomiting and swaddling
overview: This amud keeps working through the משנה about bathing and healing on שבת. First the גמרא shows that rinsing the whole body is allowed even לכתחילה, following רבי שמעון. It then explains the towel rules: one person may not carry even slightly damp towels, but a group may carry even a soaked one, because they remind each other not to wring it. אביי asks for the הלכה, and רב יוסף lists four lenient authorities: רבי שמעון, רבי, שמואל and רבי יוחנן. The גמרא also answers a challenge to רבי יוחנן from his own rule about a סתם משנה. Next come rules on moving clothes by wearing them, and on oiling the stomach differently from a weekday. The גמרא then discusses the healing baths of דיומסת, including the story of רבי אלעזר בן ערך, who lost his learning there, and the lesson of רבי נהוראי to go to a place of תורה. Finally it explains the משנה's rules on scraping, muddy rivers, inducing vomiting and swaddling a baby. It begins a statement of שמואל about resetting a broken bone, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Rinsing the whole body is allowed even from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an inference from the משנה's wording: pouring water over one's whole body is permitted even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: …which shows that rinsing one's entire body is fine even from the outset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a point it started on the previous amud. From the משנה's wording, it concludes that rinsing the whole body by pouring water is allowed even לכתחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only discussed someone who already bathed (רוחץ), which sounds like an after-the-fact case. The inference is that the problem is only with real bathing, while rinsing is a lighter activity and is allowed outright. This conclusion sets up the next question of whose opinion this is.

keyTerms.meaning: to rinse oneself by pouring water over the body, as opposed to bathing
from the outset, as an initial permission

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse רחיצה (bathing in the normal way) with שטיפה (rinsing by pouring water). The leniency here is only about rinsing.

phrases.english: that to rinse one's entire body
phrases.notes: This finishes a point the גמרא started on the previous amud.

phrases.english: even from the outset is perfectly fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְהִשְׁתַּטֵּף כׇּל גּוּפוֹ אֲפִילּוּ לְכַתְּחִילָּה שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an inference from the משנה that began on the previous amud
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the משנה, rinsing the whole body on שבת is permitted even לכתחילה.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that rinsing is allowed even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא our משנה follows. This is a setup line that prepares for the answer coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every תנא allows rinsing, so the גמרא wants to pin down the source. Knowing whose view the משנה follows tells us whether the משנה matches the majority or a single opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? (Which תנא is the author?)

phrases.english: Whose (view) is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the view just inferred
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that full-body rinsing is permitted even לכתחילה

steps.title: It is the view of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רבי שמעון permits rinsing in every case, including with hot water. The proof is the ברייתא quoted in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: it is (the view of) רבי שמעון

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of authorship

steps.title: The ברייתא with three views on rinsing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records three views: רבי מאיר forbids all rinsing, רבי שמעון permits it, and רבי יהודה forbids hot water but permits cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: A person may not rinse himself on שבת, neither with hot water nor with cold water. This is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי שמעון permits it. רבי יהודה says: with hot water it is forbidden, and with cold water it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי שמעון is the one who allows rinsing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר forbids rinsing completely, and רבי יהודה forbids it with hot water. A משנה that permits rinsing, even in hot springs, can therefore only match רבי שמעון. The three views form a clear spectrum from strict to lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: On rinsing on שבת: רבי מאיר forbids hot and cold, רבי יהודה forbids hot but permits cold, and רבי שמעון permits both. Our משנה follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: As it was taught: A person may not rinse himself
whether with hot water or with cold water,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Shimon permits it.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
With hot water it is forbidden; with cold water it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the answer that the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.raayaObject: That the leniency on full-body rinsing belongs to רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the views of רבי מאיר, רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה

steps.title: Both halves of the towel rule teach something new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase about drying with ten towels and states that both the first clause and the second clause each teach a חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And he dried himself even with ten towels.' The first clause teaches a novelty, and the second clause teaches a novelty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה about drying with towels. It announces that both parts of that rule teach something new, and it explains each part in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has a רישא: one person who dried himself, even with ten towels, may not carry them home. It also has a סיפא: ten people who dried themselves with one towel may carry it. The גמרא is about to show that neither clause is obvious, so each one is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: it teaches us a novelty (a חידוש)

phrases.english: 'And he dried himself even with ten towels.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here to start a new topic.

phrases.english: The first clause teaches us a novelty,
and the latter clause teaches us a novelty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the משנה (drying with towels)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both clauses of the towel rule contain a separate חידוש

steps.title: The first clause: even barely damp towels are forbidden for one person
steps.stepSummary: The רישא teaches that one person may not carry even towels with little water in them, because he may come to wring them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause teaches a novelty: even these towels, which do not have much water in them, are forbidden. Since he is one person, he may come to squeeze them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the חידוש of the first clause about a single person using ten towels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ten towels, each one is only slightly wet, so one might think there is no worry about wringing. The משנה still forbids carrying them, because a lone person has nobody to remind him and might squeeze them out, which is סחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: wringing or squeezing out liquid, a forbidden act on שבת

phrases.english: The first clause teaches us a novelty:

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲפִילּוּ הָנֵי דְּלָא נְפִישִׁי בְּהוּ מַיָּא,
phrases.english: that even these, which do not have much water in them,
since he is one person,
he may come to wringing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא רְבוּתָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דַּאֲפִילּוּ הָנֵי דְּלָא נְפִישִׁי בְּהוּ מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first of the two חידושים just announced
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One person may not carry even lightly damp towels, since he may wring them

steps.title: The second clause: even a very wet towel is allowed for many people
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא teaches that ten people may carry even a soaked towel, because a group reminds each other not to wring it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the latter clause teaches a novelty: even these, which have a lot of water in them, are permitted. Since they are many people, they remind one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the חידוש of the second clause about ten people sharing one towel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A towel used by ten people is very wet, so one would expect a strong worry about wringing. The משנה still permits carrying it, because in a group someone will remind the others not to squeeze it. The deciding factor is the number of people, not the amount of water.
steps.whatToRemember: The concern of wringing depends on whether a person is alone or in a group, not on how wet the towel is. Alone, even slightly damp towels are forbidden. In a group, even a soaked towel is allowed.

phrases.english: And the latter clause teaches us a novelty:
even these, which have a lot of water in them,
since they are many people,
they remind one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסֵיפָא רְבוּתָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, אֲפִילּוּ הָנֵי דִּנְפִישִׁי בְּהוּ מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the second חידוש, in contrast to the first
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Many people may carry even a very wet towel, since they remind each other not to wring it

steps.title: A ברייתא: leave the towel in the window, not with the attendants
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may dry off with a towel and leave it in the bathhouse window, but may not hand it to the bath attendants, who are suspected of wringing towels.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person may dry himself with a towel and place it in the window. He may not hand it over to the bath attendants, because they are suspected of that very thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about what to do with a towel after drying off on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the towel in the window avoids carrying it home, where he might wring it. Handing it to the attendants is forbidden because they routinely wring out towels and might do so on שבת on his behalf.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A person may dry himself with a towel
and place it in the window.
But he may not hand it over to the bath attendants,
because they are suspected of that very thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִסְתַּפֵּג אָדָם בַּאֲלוּנְטִית וּמַנִּיחָהּ בַּחַלּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא about handling a used towel
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leave the towel in the window; do not give it to the attendants, who are suspected of wringing

steps.title: רבי שמעון: he may carry one towel home
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that a person may dry off with one towel and carry it home in his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: A person may dry himself with one towel and bring it in his hand into his house.
steps.whatsHappening: In the same ברייתא, רבי שמעון gives a more lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion keeps the towel at the bathhouse because of the worry of wringing. רבי שמעון is not concerned that a lone person will wring a single towel, so he lets him carry it home. This disagrees with the strict ruling of our משנה about one person.

keyTerms.meaning: and brings it in his hand

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
One may dry himself with a single towel
and bring it in his hand into his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִסְתַּפֵּג בַּאֲלוּנְטִית אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting, more lenient view within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One person may carry a single used towel home

steps.title: אביי asks what the הלכה is
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף what the practical הלכה is on carrying a used towel home.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: What is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing the dispute, אביי asks his teacher רב יוסף which view we follow in practice. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two positions: forbidding a lone person from carrying the towel, and רבי שמעון's leniency. אביי wants to know how to actually rule.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What is the halakha?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: הִלְכְתָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical ruling on the dispute just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה permits carrying a used towel home

steps.title: רב יוסף lists four lenient authorities
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers by naming רבי שמעון, רבי, שמואל and רבי יוחנן, all of whom are lenient, which implies the הלכה permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Here is רבי שמעון, here is רבי, here is שמואל, here is רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers indirectly by naming four great authorities who all take the lenient position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of saying 'it is permitted,' רב יוסף points out that רבי שמעון, רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא), שמואל and רבי יוחנן all permit it. With so many weighty authorities agreeing, the practical ruling is to be lenient and allow carrying the towel home.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: In practice we are lenient: one may carry a towel home after drying off, because רבי שמעון, רבי, שמואל and רבי יוחנן all permit it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' alone does not mean 'some rabbi.' It refers specifically to רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic way the גמרא settles הלכה: by showing that a lenient view is backed by several major authorities, so the strict view is set aside.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Here is Rabbi Shimon, here is Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi),
here is Shmuel, here is Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָא רַבִּי, הָא שְׁמוּאֵל, הָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question about the הלכה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Four major authorities are lenient, so the הלכה permits carrying the towel home

steps.title: Source for רבי שמעון's leniency
steps.stepSummary: The source for רבי שמעון's view is the statement already quoted above.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון: that is what we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes through the four names רב יוסף listed and shows the source for each. For רבי שמעון, it points back to the ruling quoted earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, רבי שמעון already ruled that a person may dry off with a towel and carry it home. So no new source is needed. The גמרא simply says 'as we said.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon – that which we said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins backing up the list of lenient authorities from Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון permits carrying a used towel home.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's ruling quoted in Step 9.

steps.title: Source for רבי's leniency: the towels at תקוע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי and his fellow students carried oil and towels across connected areas to a spring where they bathed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי: as a ברייתא teaches. רבי said: When we studied Torah with רבי שמעון in תקוע, we would bring up oil and a towel from the courtyard to the roof, and from the roof to an enclosed area, until we reached a spring where we would bathe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי is also lenient. He describes how the students carried towels to and from the spring on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They moved only through areas where carrying is allowed: courtyard, roof and enclosure. They never passed through a public domain. Since they carried the towel to the spring, they would also carry it back after drying off, so רבי allows carrying a used towel.

keyTerms.meaning: תקוע, the town where רבי שמעון taught
An enclosed area, like a fenced yard

phrases.english: Rabbi – as it was taught: Rabbi said:
When we were learning Torah
with Rabbi Shimon in Tekoa,
we would bring up oil and a towel
from courtyard to roof and from roof to enclosure,
until we would reach a spring
in which we would bathe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second name on רב יוסף's list, now with its source.
steps.raayaObject: רבי permits carrying a towel to the bath and back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי's personal practice in תקוע.

steps.title: Source for שמואל's leniency
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explicitly allows a person to dry off with a towel and carry it home in his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל: as רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A person may dry himself with a towel and bring it in his hand into his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל openly permits carrying a used towel home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a direct ruling, so nothing has to be inferred. It matches רבי שמעון's wording exactly.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוּאֵל — דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Shmuel – as Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A person may dry himself with a towel
and bring it in his hand into his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל — דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third name on the list.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל permits carrying a used towel home.

steps.title: Source for רבי יוחנן's leniency
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה is that one may dry off with a towel and carry it home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן: as רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה is that a person may dry himself with a towel and bring it in his hand into his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the last source: רבי יוחנן says this is the actual הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן adds the word הלכה, so his statement is a practical ruling and not just one opinion. That makes it the strongest source on the list. It also sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Student who reports רבי יוחנן's rulings

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן — דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan – as Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha is: a person may dry himself with a towel
and bring it in his hand into his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן — דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth and final name on the list.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן rules this as practical הלכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא בר אבא's report of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: All four authorities, רבי שמעון, רבי, שמואל and רבי יוחנן, allow carrying a used towel home on שבת.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן contradict his own rule?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה, and our משנה forbids carrying even ten towels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? Didn't רבי יוחנן say the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה? And we learned: 'If he dried himself even with ten towels, he may not bring them in his hand!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling. His own general rule seems to force the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a rule that a משנה quoted without a name is the הלכה. Our משנה forbids carrying the towels and gives no name. So by his own rule, he should forbid carrying them.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed משנה, stated without a name

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say so?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The halacha follows an unattributed mishna,
and we learned: 'and he dried himself'
even with ten towels,
he may not bring them in his hand!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source just quoted for רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling on carrying a towel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own rule says to follow an unattributed משנה, and the unattributed משנה forbids carrying.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's version credits the משנה to בן חכינאי
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יוחנן's text, that משנה was taught in the name of בן חכינאי, so it is not unattributed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one: he taught it as the view of בן חכינאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in רבי יוחנן's version of the משנה, the strict ruling carries the name of a single sage, בן חכינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rule only applies to a משנה with no name attached. Here the strict view belongs to one individual sage, so רבי יוחנן is free to rule leniently.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches it, meaning this is his version of the text

phrases.english: That one – he teaches it as following ben Chachinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The strict משנה is unattributed and binding by רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רבי יוחנן's text it is attributed to בן חכינאי, an individual, so it is not binding.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה allows carrying a used towel home. The strict משנה is a minority view.

steps.title: Bath attendants may bring women's bathing garments by wearing them
steps.stepSummary: Bath attendants may bring women's bath garments to the bathhouse if they wear them, covering their heads and most of their bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Bath attendants may bring women's bath garments to the bathhouse, as long as they cover their heads and most of their bodies with them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new related ruling: you may move clothing on שבת by actually wearing it, not by carrying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying clothing in your hands through a public area is forbidden. But if you wear it, covering your head and most of your body, it counts as clothing you are dressed in.

keyTerms.meaning: Their heads and most of their bodies

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Bath attendants may bring women's bathing garments
to the bathhouse,
provided that they cover with them
their heads and most of their bodies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָאוֹלְיָירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling about moving garments to and from the bathhouse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garments may be moved by wearing them, covering the head and most of the body.

steps.title: A large scarf must be tied below
steps.stepSummary: A large shoulder scarf must have its two ends tied below so that it is worn properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: A large scarf: one must tie its two ends below.
steps.whatsHappening: Another rule about wearing rather than carrying: a big draped scarf must be tied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loose draped scarf might slip off, and the person might then carry it. Tying the ends keeps it firmly worn. The next step explains where 'below' means.

keyTerms.meaning: A large scarf draped over the shoulders

phrases.english: A large scarf – one must tie
its two ends below.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִכְנִיתָא צָרִיךְ לְקַשֵּׁר שְׁנֵי רָאשֶׁיהָ לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of wearing garments properly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scarf's ends must be tied below so it is securely worn.

steps.title: 'Below' means below the shoulders
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the scarf must be tied below the shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: below the shoulders.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן clarifies the word 'below' from the previous ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying the scarf below the shoulders makes it hang and sit like a real garment. That is why it does not count as carrying.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Below the shoulders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְמַטָּה מִכְּתֵפַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a word in the previous ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scarf is tied below the shoulders.

steps.title: רבא's instruction to the people of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא told the people of מחוזא to wear soldiers' garments extended below their shoulders when moving them on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to the people of מחוזא: When you move clothing for the soldiers, let it hang down on you below the shoulders.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies the same idea in practice. Clothing brought to soldiers must be worn properly, not carried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the scarf, the garment has to reach below the shoulders so that it is worn the normal way. This turns moving it into wearing it.

phrases.english: Rava said to the people of Mechoza:
When you transport garments for the soldiers,
let them extend below the shoulders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'below the shoulders' rule in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Transported garments must be worn extending below the shoulders.
steps.whatToRemember: Clothing may be moved on שבת by truly wearing it, covering most of the body or hanging below the shoulders.

steps.title: Smearing oil and rubbing the stomach, unlike a weekday
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא permits smearing oil on and rubbing the stomach on שבת, but not the way it is done during the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may smear oil and rub.' The רבנן taught: One may smear oil on and rub the stomach area on שבת, as long as he does not do it the way he does on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a phrase from the משנה and quotes a ברייתא about it. The ברייתא adds a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rubbing oil on the stomach could look like medical treatment, which is restricted on שבת. It is allowed only if it is done in a way that looks different from the usual weekday treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: The way one does it on a weekday

phrases.english: 'One may smear oil and rub.'
The Rabbis taught: One may smear oil and rub
the intestinal area on Shabbat,
provided that he not do it
the way he does on a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oiling and rubbing the stomach is allowed on שבת, but only in a manner that differs from weekdays.

steps.title: How is it done differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the different, שבת-style method is.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for practical detail. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said to change the method but did not say how. The question asks what that change looks like.

phrases.english: How does he do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the ברייתא's condition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What counts as a non-weekday way of oiling and rubbing.

steps.title: רבי חמא בר חנינא: smear first, then rub
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא says one smears the oil first and rubs afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא said: He smears oil, and afterward he rubs.
steps.whatsHappening: First answer: do the two actions one after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, on a weekday the oiling and rubbing are done together. Splitting them into separate steps makes it look different.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said:
He smears oil and afterward rubs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: smear and rub at once
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says one smears and rubs at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: He smears oil and rubs at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: Second answer: do both actions together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, on a weekday one smears first and then rubs. So doing both together is the change. The two אמוראים disagree about what the normal weekday method is.
steps.confusionAlert: The two opinions are not arguing about whether a change is needed. Both agree it is. They disagree only about which method is the normal weekday one, so the 'change' is opposite in each view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
He smears oil and rubs at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר סָךְ וּמְמַשְׁמֵשׁ בְּבַת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing answer to the same question.
steps.whatToRemember: Oiling the stomach on שבת must be done differently from a weekday. רבי חמא בר חנינא says to do it in sequence, and רבי יוחנן says to do it all at once.

steps.title: Not even standing on the floor of the healing baths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'but one may not exert oneself.' רבי יוחנן says this means one may not even stand on the floor of the baths of דיומסת on שבת, because the place itself warms and heals.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But one may not exert oneself.' רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is forbidden to stand on the floor of דיומסת, because it warms the body and heals it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה. רבי יוחנן explains them with a case: even just standing in the healing baths of דיומסת is forbidden on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids exerting oneself to sweat, because that is a kind of healing. רבי יוחנן adds that at דיומסת you do not even need to exert yourself. The hot floor heats the body and heals by itself, so just standing there is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: exert oneself, work up a sweat for health
דיומסת, famous natural hot baths with healing power
it warms (makes one sweat) and heals

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's case does not involve bathing or exercising at all. The point is that at דיומסת, standing there is already the forbidden 'exertion.'

phrases.english: But one may not exert oneself.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is forbidden to stand on the floor of Deyomset
because it warms and heals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה after the discussion of rubbing in oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת it is forbidden even to stand on the floor of דיומסת, because the place itself causes healing sweat.

steps.title: The healing season of the baths is twenty-one days
steps.stepSummary: רב says the baths of דיומסת heal during a 21-day season, and עצרת is counted as one of those days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The whole healing season of דיומסת is twenty-one days, and עצרת is counted among them.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא is already talking about דיומסת, it adds a fact about it. The baths only heal during a set 21-day period that includes עצרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us the healing power is seasonal and not active all year. Saying 'עצרת is counted' fixes the period around שבועות. It does not say where in the 21 days עצרת falls, and that gap sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: part of the count, included in the number

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
All the (healing) days of Deyomset
are twenty-one days,
and Shavuot is included in the count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds background about the same baths mentioned by רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דיומסת heals for 21 days, and עצרת is one of them.

steps.title: Is שבועות at the start or the end of the period?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether עצרת is the first day of the 21-day season or the last.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is עצרת at the beginning, on this side, or on that side, at the end?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רב's statement. Is עצרת the start of the 21 days or the end?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said עצרת is 'included' but did not say where. If it comes first, the season runs after שבועות, during the hotter days. If it comes last, the season runs in the 21 days before שבועות.

keyTerms.meaning: they asked a question (a real open question)

phrases.english: They asked:
Is Shavuot at the start, on this side,
or on that side (at the end)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a detail that רב's statement left unclear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether עצרת is the first day or the last day of the 21-day healing period.

steps.title: A possible proof from medicinal drinks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer from שמואל, who said medicinal drinks work from פסח until עצרת. That would suggest the healing season ends at עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, since שמואל said: All medicinal drinks work well from פסח until עצרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question with a statement of שמואל about medicinal drinks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says healing drinks work in the period leading up to עצרת. If the baths work the same way, their 21 days would also come before עצרת, which would make עצרת the last day.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear, an attempted proof

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Shmuel said:
All medicinal drinks
from Passover until Shavuot are effective!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of Step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That עצרת is the end of the 21-day bath season.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל: medicinal drinks work from פסח until עצרת.

steps.title: Drinks need cool weather, baths need heat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Drinks work better when the weather is cool, but the baths heal through heat, so they work better when the weather is warm.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps there, with drinks, the cooler the world is, the better they work. But here the healing comes from heat, so the warmer the world is, the better it works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. Drinks and baths are different, so we cannot learn one from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drinks heal best in the cooler weeks before שבועות. The baths heal through heat, so their season may come in the warmer weeks after שבועות. The question is left without an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps, the opening of a rejection

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from שמואל fails because drinks and hot baths heal in opposite kinds of weather. The question about עצרת stays open.

phrases.english: Perhaps there it is so
because the cooler the world, the more effective (the drinks are);
but here it is because of the heat,
so when the world is warm, it is more effective.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between medicinal drinks and the baths.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Drinks heal best in cool weather, while baths heal through heat and work best in warm weather.

steps.title: Wine and baths caused the loss of the ten tribes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו says the wine of פרוגיתא and the waters of דיומסת caused the ten tribes to be lost to Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said: The wine of פרוגיתא and the water of דיומסת cut off the ten tribes from Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא mentioned דיומסת, it brings an aggadic teaching about it. Pleasure-seeking there led the ten tribes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that being drawn after physical pleasures like fine wine and luxury baths pulled the tribes away from תורה, and so they were lost. This prepares the story that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: פרוגיתא (Phrygia), a region famous for its wine

phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said:
The wine of Phrygia and the water of Deyomset
deprived Israel of the ten tribes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from הלכה to aggadah, connected by the word דיומסת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pleasures of פרוגיתא's wine and דיומסת's baths led to the loss of the ten tribes.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן ערך forgets his learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן ערך went to that place, was drawn after its pleasures, and forgot his תורה. When he came back, he misread a פסוק so badly that the רבנן had to pray for him, and his learning returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן ערך came there and was drawn after them, and his learning was uprooted. When he returned, he got up to read from the ספר תורה. He was supposed to read 'הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם', but he read 'הַחֵרֵשׁ הָיָה לִבָּם'. The רבנן prayed for him, and his learning came back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows how dangerous the pleasures of that place were, even for a great חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He forgot so much that he mixed up letters that look alike: ד/ר, ז/י, כ/ב. So 'This month shall be for you' became 'Was their heart deaf?' The misreading itself describes what had happened to him, and only the רבנן's prayers restored his learning.
steps.confusionAlert: 'הַחֵרֵשׁ הָיָה לִבָּם' is not a real פסוק. It is his mistaken reading of 'הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם', made by swapping letters that look alike.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ אִיקְּלַע לְהָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh happened to come there;
he was drawn after them,
and his learning was uprooted.
When he came back,
he stood up to read from the Torah scroll;
he was supposed to read: 'This month shall be for you,'
but he said: 'Was their heart deaf?'
The Sages prayed for mercy for him,
and his learning returned.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ אִיקְּלַע לְהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of רבי חלבו's warning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a great חכם can lose his תורה by being drawn after pleasures and leaving the company of תורה scholars.

steps.title: The story explains the teaching of רבי נהוראי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the story to the משנה where רבי נהוראי teaches: go into exile to a place of תורה. Do not assume it will follow you, because your friends are the ones who keep it firm in your hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is what we learned in a משנה. רבי נהוראי says: Go into exile to a place of תורה, and do not say it will come after you. Your colleagues are the ones who will make it last in your hands. And do not rely on your own understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the story fits a known משנה about going to a place of תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן ערך went to a place without תורה scholars and lost his learning. רבי נהוראי's lesson is that תורה stays with you through learning with friends, not through trusting your own mind alone.

keyTerms.meaning: and that is what we learned (in a משנה)
will establish it (make it last) in your hands

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known lesson in Jewish life: a person needs a community of learners in order to keep his תורה.

phrases.english: And this is what we learned: Rabbi Nehorai says:
Exile yourself to a place of Torah,
and do not say that it will come after you,
for your colleagues will establish it in your hands,
and do not rely on your own understanding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the story of Step 32 to a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The lesson of the רבי אלעזר בן ערך story.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of רבי נהוראי: go into exile to a place of תורה.

steps.title: Who רבי נהוראי really was
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says 'רבי נהוראי' was not his real name. His name was רבי נחמיה, and some say it was רבי אלעזר בן ערך himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי נהוראי was not his name. Rather, רבי נחמיה was his name. And some say רבי אלעזר בן ערך was his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the identity of רבי נהוראי. One opinion says he was the same רבי אלעזר בן ערך from the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי נהוראי is רבי אלעזר בן ערך, then the משנה's lesson comes from his own painful experience. That makes the link between the story and the משנה even stronger.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Nehorai was not his name,
rather, Rabbi Nechemya was his name.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ שְׁמוֹ.
phrases.english: And some say Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh was his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies who said the משנה quoted in Step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נהוראי was really רבי נחמיה, or, according to another opinion, רבי אלעזר בן ערך.

steps.title: Why was he called נהוראי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he was called רבי נהוראי if that was not his real name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was he called רבי נהוראי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question that sets up the explanation of the nickname.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his real name was something else, the name נהוראי must have a reason behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: and why was he called by this name

phrases.english: And why was he called Rabbi Nehorai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the name change in Step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the nickname נהוראי.

steps.title: He lit up the eyes of the Sages
steps.stepSummary: He was called נהוראי, from the word for light, because he lit up the eyes of the חכמים in הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he would light up the eyes of the חכמים in הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The name נהוראי means 'light,' because he brought clarity to the חכמים in הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נהוראי comes from נהורא, which means light. The nickname was a title of honor for his clear teaching of הלכה.
steps.whatToRemember: The section ends with a warning about pleasures that pull a person away from תורה, and a lesson to stay close to a place of תורה and to fellow learners.

phrases.english: Because he would illuminate the eyes of the Sages in halakha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name נהוראי comes from 'light,' because he lit up the eyes of the חכמים in הלכה.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids scraping the body with a scraper on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'but one may not scrape.' It then brings a ברייתא that says one may not scrape the body with a scraper on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'But one may not scrape.' The רבנן taught: One may not scrape with a scraper on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and picks up its next phrase, 'one may not scrape.' It brings a ברייתא that spells out the rule: no scraping the body with a scraper on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'no scraping.' The ברייתא adds what the scraping is done with: a מגררת, a scraping tool used in the bathhouse to clean oil and dirt off the skin. This sets up the general rule, and the next step brings an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Scraping oneself (cleaning the skin by scraping it)
A scraper, a bathhouse tool for scraping the skin clean
'The רבנן taught,' the opening words of a ברייתא

phrases.english: (The mishna said:) But one may not scrape oneself.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, opening a new topic.

phrases.english: The Sages taught (in a baraita):
One may not scrape with a scraper on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי נהוראי discussion and goes back to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not use a scraper on one's body on שבת.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows scraping feet covered in mud or filth
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if a person's feet are dirty with mud or filth, he may scrape them in his usual way and does not need to worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If his feet were dirty with mud and filth, he may scrape them the normal way and need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives an exception to the rule against scraping: feet covered in mud or filth may be scraped as usual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is aimed at ordinary, bathhouse-style scraping for comfort. When the feet are actually filthy, cleaning them is a real need, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows it with no hesitation ('ואינו חושש').

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he need not worry' (there is no problem)

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If his feet were dirty
with mud and with excrement,
he may scrape in his usual way and need not be concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the ברייתא's ban on scraping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feet dirty with mud or filth may be scraped normally on שבת.

steps.title: רב שמואל בר יהודה's mother made him a silver scraper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells that רב שמואל בר יהודה's mother made him a scraper out of silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יהודה's mother made him a silver scraper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short story: רב שמואל בר יהודה's mother made him a scraper of silver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows how scraping was handled in practice. Rashi says it was made 'לשבת', for שבת. A special silver scraper made the שבת scraping different from weekday scraping.

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda:
his mother made for him
a scraper of silver.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה עֲבַדָא לֵיהּ אִימֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life story about scraping that closes the scraping topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A special silver scraper was made, showing how scraping was done in a changed way.

steps.title: Why may one not go down into a muddy river?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that one may not go down into a קורדימא, a muddy river, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not go down into a קורדימא,' and so on. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next rule in the משנה, the ban on going into a muddy river, and asks why. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply going into water is not one of the forbidden מלאכות. So the גמרא wants to know what the real worry is.

phrases.english: (The mishna said:) One may not go down into a swampy river, etc.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason going into a muddy river is forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: Because of the mud
steps.stepSummary: The answer: it is forbidden because of the mud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the mud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the problem is the mud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mud is slippery, so the person may slip and fall into the water. Then he may come to bathe or to wring out his soaked clothes, which is forbidden. The ban is a safeguard, not a ban on going into water itself.

phrases.english: Because of the mud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 40.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mud may make him slip and fall in, which can lead to wringing out clothes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only vomiting with a drug is forbidden, not by hand
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says one may not make oneself vomit on שבת. רבי יוחנן, quoted by רבה בר בר חנה, says this applies only to using a drug. Making oneself vomit by hand is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not make oneself vomit on שבת.' רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They only taught this about a drug. But by hand, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next rule in the משנה, about making oneself vomit, and רבי יוחנן narrows it to using a drug.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A drug counts as medicine, and medicine on שבת is restricted. Making oneself vomit by hand involves no medicine, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this about,' a phrase that limits a rule

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה forbids every kind of vomiting on שבת. רבי יוחנן says it forbids only the drug method. Vomiting by hand is allowed.

phrases.english: (The mishna said:) And one may not induce vomiting on Shabbat.
Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They only taught this with regard to a drug,
but by hand, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּסַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new rule in the משנה and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making oneself vomit with a drug is forbidden on שבת, but doing it by hand is permitted.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: needless vomiting is forbidden even on a weekday
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי נחמיה: making oneself vomit is forbidden even on a weekday because it wastes food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי נחמיה says: Even on a weekday it is forbidden, because it wastes food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי נחמיה adds a separate reason not to make oneself vomit, one that applies even on weekdays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ban has nothing to do with שבת. Throwing up food without a medical need destroys good food, and that is wasteful. So רבי נחמיה forbids it every day of the week.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Neḥemya says:
Even on a weekday it is prohibited,
because of the loss of food.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: אַף בַּחוֹל אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate, weekday reason against vomiting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making oneself vomit without need is forbidden even on a weekday, because it wastes food.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: swaddling a baby on שבת is fine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says one may not straighten a baby's body on שבת. רבי יוחנן, quoted by רבה בר בר חנה, says that swaddling a baby on שבת is perfectly fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not straighten a baby.' רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Swaddling a baby on שבת is perfectly fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next rule in the משנה, about straightening a baby's body, and brings רבי יוחנן's ruling that swaddling is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swaddling means wrapping a baby tightly, which also helps the body grow straight. So רבי יוחנן's permission seems to clash with the משנה's ban on straightening a baby. The next step raises exactly that problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Straightening a baby's body or limbs

phrases.english: (The mishna said:) And one may not straighten a baby.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
To swaddle a baby on Shabbat
is perfectly fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לַפּוֹפֵי יָנוֹקָא בְּשַׁבָּת שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next rule of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swaddling a baby on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: But the משנה says not to straighten a baby!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: the משנה itself says one may not straighten a baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: 'One may not straighten a baby'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's permission by pointing to the משנה's ban on straightening a baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swaddling also shapes and straightens the baby's body. If the משנה forbids straightening, how can רבי יוחנן allow swaddling?

keyTerms.meaning: 'But we learned (in a משנה),' introducing a challenge

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the mishna:
One may not straighten (a baby)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 44.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's permission to swaddle a baby on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Swaddling straightens the baby, and the משנה forbids straightening a baby.

steps.title: The משנה means straightening the spine, which looks like building
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about straightening the bones of the spine. That looks like building, so it is forbidden. Ordinary swaddling is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the משנה is talking about the vertebrae of the spine, because straightening them looks like building.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem: the משנה's ban covers only setting the spine. Plain swaddling is still permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lining up the spine's vertebrae one on top of another looks like assembling a structure, which resembles the מלאכה of בונה. Swaddling just wraps the baby and does not look like building. So רבי יוחנן and the משנה do not conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: Building, one of the forbidden מלאכות of שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Swaddling a baby on שבת is permitted. Straightening a baby's spine is forbidden because it looks like בונה.

phrases.english: There, it refers to the vertebrae of the spine,
because it looks like building.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 45 by limiting what the משנה refers to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers to the spine only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's ban covers any straightening of a baby, including swaddling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban covers only setting the spine, which looks like בונה. Swaddling is permitted.

steps.title: The משנה's clause on resetting a broken bone, and the start of שמואל's comment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that one may not reset a broken bone on שבת. It then starts to bring a statement of שמואל, reported by רבי חנא בגדתאה. The statement itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one may not reset a broken bone on שבת. רבי חנא בגדתאה said in the name of שמואל: (his statement follows on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next clause of the משנה, the rule against resetting a broken bone on שבת. It is setting up the next move by introducing a comment from שמואל, which will be stated right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as Steps 42 and 44. There, the גמרא quoted a clause of the משנה and then brought an אמורא who explained how far that clause reaches. Here we only get the clause and the chain of who said it. שמואל's actual ruling about this clause has not been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: We put back / reset (here: putting a broken bone back into place)
A break, meaning a broken bone
רבי חנא of Baghdad, who passes on שמואל's teaching
A leading early Babylonian אמורא, whose statement is being introduced

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking the משנה's ban is the final word. The line 'אמר רבי חנא בגדתאה אמר שמואל' is only an opening. שמואל's statement, which comes next, is the real point of this step.

phrases.english: And one may not reset a break (a broken bone).
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, the next item in its list of healing activities forbidden on שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥana of Baghdad said
phrases.notes: He is the one who passes on the teaching.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: This is the source of the teaching. The statement itself continues on the next amud.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup / attribution line introducing a מימרא
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מַחֲזִירִין אֶת הַשֶּׁבֶר. אָמַר רַבִּי חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of straightening a baby (Steps 44-46), the גמרא moves to the next clause of the same משנה, resetting a broken bone. It uses the same 'quote the clause, then bring an אמורא' pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה forbids resetting a broken bone on שבת. שמואל's comment on this clause, reported by רבי חנא בגדתאה, is about to be stated.
